evidence: Reviewed bin/labdrian-overlay's new reconcile block in cmd_capture (fetch + ff-only/merge origin/upstream, die on conflict); only fixed branch/remote literals used, no injectable/untrusted input, no secrets, no auth logic changed.

Reviewed new file tui/capture_backend_test.go in full: hermetic Go test harness using t.TempDir() and fixed exec.Command arguments; no attacker-controlled input, no secrets, no new dependencies introduced.

findings.claim: The die() path on a real merge conflict leaves MERGE_HEAD set on 'upstream'; simply re-running capture re-enters the same merge logic while MERGE_HEAD is still present, which git rejects with 'You have not concluded your merge', reproducing the same generic die message instead of guiding the user to run git merge --abort or commit first.
proof_refs: bin/labdrian-overlay:625-626 unconditionally reruns git merge --no-edit origin/upstream on every capture invocation with no MERGE_HEAD check first
bin/labdrian-overlay:626 die message never mentions git merge --abort or committing the resolution before retrying

findings.claim: When git merge --ff-only succeeds directly (the common case), the reconcile step silently advances local upstream with no log line, while the rarer merge path logs an explicit Reconciled info line.
proof_refs: the info call sits only inside the if-not-ff-only block, so it never executes when git merge --ff-only succeeds directly

findings.claim: The fetch-failure graceful-degradation branch (warn and proceed without reconciling) has no regression test in this candidate.
proof_refs: bin/labdrian-overlay:630-632 is the sole fetch-failure fallback branch added by this diff
